_meta.purpose: Machine-readable retraction registry. A retracted VALUE is listed here ONCE; audit_stale.py then finds every document that still quotes it without a supersession stamp. This is what makes 'invalidate and forward-reference' checkable instead of a discipline nobody can verify.
_meta.why: User, 2026-09-04: 'I'm still worried about stale entries that don't follow invalidate, forward-reference. However, checking for this would require visiting each entry... An O(n^2) process.' It is O(n^2) only if entries are compared with EACH OTHER. Compared against ONE registry it is O(n), and retractions are rare.
_meta.adding_one: Add the value, what it was, why it died, and what replaces it. Then run audit_stale.py — it will list every place that still asserts it.
_meta.seeding: 🔴 SEED THIS FROM KNOWN.md § NOT ESTABLISHED, not from memory. The first version was written from what I remembered of one week and MISSED the oldest and most damaging entry: coupling.beta is not mesh-converged. A registry built from recollection inherits recollection's blind spots.
_meta.naming: 🔑 EVERY quantity here carries its STATE. coupling.beta.cold and coupling.beta.loaded differ by ~450x and sit on opposite coupling branches; an unqualified 'coupling.beta' names neither. Same rule as cavity.Q_ext.cold (CONVENTIONS §7.1).

retractions.was: coupling.beta quoted as a measured coupling coefficient
retractions.why: NOT MESH-CONVERGED. 2026-08-23: beta moved 43.1% for a 1.25x linear refinement (0.4081 -> 0.2320) and was still falling. Q0 = Q_L(1+beta) moved 0.12% over the same refinement — beta and Q_L COMPENSATE, so Q0 is stable and beta is not. Q_ext = Q0/beta inherits beta's instability in full. All 2026-09-03/04 runs used size_factor 1.5, the COARSEST point of the declared series. ⚠️ THE WARNING ITSELF IS UNDERSPECIFIED: it does not say COLD or LOADED, and beta.cold (112, overcoupled) and beta.loaded (0.25, undercoupled) are not the same quantity. Its figures (0.4081 -> 0.2320) appear in ONE line of OPTIMIZER.md with no slug and no artefact, and predate branch resolution (h3_driven hardcoded the UNDERCOUPLED root until 2026-08-24), so they are probably the wrong root of a cold overcoupled case — on the other branch the same pair is a 76% move, not 43%. Treat 'beta is not converged' as the claim; do NOT quote 43%.
retractions.superseded_by: MEASURED at FOUR resolutions on the design cavity (barrel mount, gap2 2.25 mm, loop 11x8, plasma.n_e 7.9e18, driven): coupling.beta.loaded = 0.2476 (sf 1.5) / 0.2882 (1.2) / 0.3007 (1.0) / 0.3264 (0.8). 🔴 STILL NOT CONVERGED, and the 2026-09-04 reading of it was too optimistic: the step is NON-MONOTONE (+16.41%, +4.35%, +8.56%) — the LAST refinement moved beta about twice as far as the one before, so 'still moving 4.3% at the finest resolution' understated it. cavity.Q_ext.loaded tracks it: 305.3 / 260.1 / 249.3 / 227.6 (-8.7% on the last step). ✅ cavity.Q0.loaded is STABLE TO 0.88% across the whole series (75.58 / 74.95 / 74.97 / 74.31), confirming that beta and Q_L compensate and that Q0 is the trustworthy quantity here.

retractions.was: coupling.beta.loaded = 0.2053 for the AZIMUTHAL coupler at f0 = 2.4474 GHz, design cavity, plasma.n_e 7.9e18 (h3-azimload-02)
retractions.why: THERE IS NO RESONANCE AT 2.4474 GHz IN THAT SWEEP. |S11| is a monotonic slope from -2.73 dB at 2.30 GHz to -5.25 dB at 2.58; the 'local minimum' at 2.4474 is -3.618 dB with its 2.46 GHz neighbour LOWER at -3.623 — ripple, not a dip. Decisively, the PHASE moves 0.4 deg over 20 MHz there, where a Q_L~56 resonance would rotate ~180 deg across its linewidth. beta was taken from a dip depth that is not a resonance, so it is not a coupling coefficient. The only genuine in-band feature is 2.6024 GHz at -12.388 dB.

retractions.why: THE AZIMUTHAL S11 SITS ON A 44% BROADBAND ABSORPTION PEDESTAL THAT CANNOT BE PHYSICAL. Measured baseline -2.40 dB WITH NO PLASMA (sigma=0, vacuum) against the barrel's -0.00 dB. A closed vacuum cavity with copper and aluminium surfaces cannot absorb 44% of incident power at every frequency. Conductor loss accounts for 0.46% of what is needed (arc resistance ~33 mOhm vs the ~7 Ohm implied). The solved Boundaries are IDENTICAL to the barrel's — same attribute 91, R=50, same materials, same Direction — so it is the MESH GEOMETRY (port face or loop), not the configuration. Q_L comes from a 3 dB walk on a pedestal, so every Q_ext = Q_L(1+beta)/beta inherits it. ⚠️ beta itself is SOUND: the circle fit agrees with the rig to 0.15% in both arms. 🔴 2026-09-07, MEASURED, and it overturns the mesh-error explanation: Palace SurfaceFlux Type 'Power' on the wall, port and loop shows the azimuthal model dissipates 0.4% of the claimed absorption off resonance and 23% on it, while the BARREL closes to 97% on resonance and 89% off. NOTHING IS ABSORBING. The |S11| itself is wrong. ⚠️ The error indicator being 22x the barrel's, and the pedestal falling under refinement, are CORRELATION — refinement changes how wrong the port-face integration is, not how much power is lost, because none is.
retractions.superseded_by: CAUSE IDENTIFIED: the azimuthal LUMPED PORT FACE IS NOT FLAT. The gap faces are planes at +-psi, so the port face spanning them is an annular SECTOR, and Palace's lumped port requires a flat element ('bounding box discovered length should match projected length'). geometry.py has documented this as 'the open problem' since the azimuthal loop was built. A lumped port on a non-flat face integrates the wrong voltage and current, so |S11| is wrong WITH NO POWER IMBALANCE TO NOTICE. The barrel's gap is a planar slot in a straight crossbar and is unaffected. 🔴 STILL NOTHING QUOTABLE from the azimuthal driven arm until the port face is fixed.
